messages:
anya: Quick coordination: support + eng-runtime asked for a docs change. Instead of only consolidating 429/timeout/context guidance, can we add a tiny CI job that runs the SDK snippets so they don't bitrot?
kevin: Love that. We keep getting bug reports from copy-paste snippets that don't actually run. A docs-snippet-test job in CI would help.
rachel: I can add a GH Action that pulls the small example set and runs unit checks. We'll need canonical fallback names in a lint config so tests can validate mapping (trim_context, retry_with_backoff, switch_model_variant, route_to_fallback).
anya: Also include a short code example showing structured error inspection (customers asked how to look at error.meta). Keep snippet small.
kevin: Proposed python snippet for structured errors:```python
err = response.json().get('error', {})
code = err.get('code')
meta = err.get('meta', {})
if code == 'rate_limit': handle_retry(meta.get('retry_after'))
```
rachel: Nice. I'll wire the docs CI to run that snippet in a container and fail the PR if snippet output changes. docs-ci-bot: opened PR #3906 "snippet-ci + structured-error-sample" (labels: docs, infra)
anya: Great. Please add a short troubleshooting callout: when SDK emits error.meta.retry_window vs Retry-After header, prefer header for immediate backoff but fall back to meta when headers are missing.
kevin: Add a tiny node example for reading structured error body:```js
const err = await res.json();
if (err?.error?.code === 'context_limit') {
  client.fallback.trimContext();
}
```
rachel: Scheduling quick review tomorrow 10am PT. If green, we'll merge, enable the GH Action, and add a changelog entry. Also ping #support so agents can link to the canonical page and mention that snippets are now tested.
anya: Thanks team. This should reduce a lot of repeated support churn. :sparkles:
